Subject: Post-call: RetailCo model fit & evals (quality/regression follow-up)

Hi Alex / Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: improve customer support summarization accuracy for RetailCo's returns flows (short form summaries + action item extraction).
- Current constraints: 1) tight P95 latency target (200ms), 2) enforced PII redaction, 3) strict cost envelope for production throughput.

Redwood recommendations (first-pass)
- Candidate models to evaluate: open-llama-3-7b-v1 (quantized) for cost-sensitive flows; redwood-13b-v1 (v2 quantized) for higher-quality extraction.
- Prompt sets: we've scoped a 250-example prompt evaluation (Drive link below) focusing on edge cases you flagged (embedded receipts, truncated messages).
- Benchmarks: initial evals attached (model_eval_summary_v1.pdf). See latency and ROUGE/EM metrics on page 2.

Immediate next steps
1) We’ll run a focused A/B eval across the two candidate models against your 250-case prompt set (ETA: 72 hours).
2) We’ll share diffs (per-example) and recommend pinning a model version for canary traffic.
3) If you want, we can scope a short POC that pins the chosen model for a single support queue.

Action owner / ETA
- Redwood (Marissa / Neha): deliver per-example diffs + recommended model & pin by 2027-04-04.
- RetailCo (Alex): send any additional failure examples / high-priority edge cases by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: model_eval_summary_v1.pdf (PDF)
Related: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RetailCo-Evals, https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-sets/blob/main/retailco.json

Thanks — Marissa

Hi all — quick triage update from the runtime team. TL;DR: confirmed a quality regression tied to a quantization kernel selection change on 2027-03-27; we have a rollback plan and recommended pinned version.

What we found:
- Change: On 2027-03-27 we introduced an optimized int8 kernel path that reduces per-token CPU/GPU ops for the v2 quantized pipeline. It improves latency but, at the current sampling temperature defaults, it can slightly bias logits in edge extraction cases.
- Evidence: attached per-example diffs (eval_diffs_20270403.csv) show divergence concentrated in receipts/invoice cases with nested lists.

Recommended immediate actions (can be executed within 2–6 hours):
1) Rollback option A (fast): pin production canary to redwood-13b-v1@2027-03-21 (previous kernel path). This is low-risk and reverses the observed regressions.
2) Rollforward option B (medium): keep new kernel but apply a sampling patch (lower default temperature and force-bias correction) — requires a config push and a 12–24 hour validation window.

Our recommendation: for RetailCo's POC, pin to redwood-13b-v1@2027-03-21 for the canary (option A) so they can continue evaluation. Parallel work: we will run a targeted calibration (option B) to recover latency gains without the quality hit.

Plan & ETA:
- If you approve pin (A), we can push the canary pin within 2–6 hours and provide a follow-up per-example validation report within 24 hours.
- Deliverables: rollback/pin plan doc (internal link below), updated eval diffs (attached), and suggested pinned config for your canary route.

Attachments: eval_diffs_20270403.csv
Related: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RetailCo-Evals, internal doc: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/rollback-pin-2027-03

Alex — want me to go ahead and schedule the pin for your canary? If yes, I'll coordinate the time window and notify procurement & your platform team.

Thanks — Neha
